deviation_mechanism: High curvature regularization weight (0.15) enforces excessive smoothness between adjacent layer thicknesses. In multi-layer optical designs, target performance relies on precise phase accumulation and impedance matching; forcing adjacent layers into rigid periodic patterns (e.g., candidate 1 maintains strict alternation between ~33.9 nm and ~48.9 nm) destroys the independent degree of freedom required for fine spectral tuning. This over-constraint prunes high-performing configurations from the feasible set, causing the optimizer to settle on structurally stable but optically suboptimal solutions, driving the score downward.
continue_rationale: Three rounds executed show rapid score degradation (0.503187 to 0.108559) rather than stagnation, indicating the current constraint regime is actively suppressing discoverable solutions. The search space remains accessible (`valid_candidates`=9), meaning the physics is not refuted, only the parametrization is too restrictive. Relaxing bounds and regularization will restore exploration capacity and allow verification of whether the degradation stems from bound tightness or fundamental material limits.
insight_for_next: Relax edge layer bounds from ±1.0 nm to ±2.0 nm and reduce curvature regularization weight from 0.15 to 0.08. Reinitialize thickness parameters with broader uniform perturbation ranges to break the rigid alternating thickness pattern observed in prior rounds.
